Laves phase still shows an increasing trend at Nb8. Concurrently, the volume fraction of FCC phase decreases from 98% in Nb1 to 64% in Nb8 (Fig. 2i).

The dendritic white precipitates phase is gradually connected when Nb content is 2%. At this point, Laves phase volume fraction reaches 4%.

(Co30Cr25Fe40Ni5)98Nb2 exhibited superior mechanical properties, including a compressive strength, fracture strain and hardness of 1664.88 MPa, 44.58% and 286.28 HV , respectively.
The (Co 30Cr25Fe40Ni5)98Nb2 alloy exhibited excellent performance overall, with a strength of 1664.88 MPa, a strain rate of 44.58%, and a hardness of 286.28 HV .

With the Nb content increases, the solid solution of Nb atoms with a large atomic radius causes a greater degree of lattice distortion in FCC phase.
Grain reﬁnement increases the total number of grain boundaries, which in turn enhances the resistance to dislocation movement and improves the strength of the studied alloys.

The excellent compressive properties of the studied alloys are attributed to solid solution strengthening of Nb atoms, reﬁnement of the eutectic layer and precipitation strengthening of Nb-rich Laves phase in FCC phase.
Part of Nb element is solidly dissolved in FCC phase to form substitutional solid solution, which leads to lattice distortion.
The main strengthening mechanism of the studied alloys was solid solution strengthening, fine grain strengthening, and precipitation strengthening.
